verses.text: Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by birth, was made ruler over the kingdom of the Babylonians.
In the first year of his rule, I, Daniel, learned from the Scriptures how many years Jerusalem would lie in ruins. The LORD had told the prophet Jeremiah that it would be seventy years.
So I turned to the Lord God and pleaded with him in prayer. I fasted, wore rough cloth, and sat in ashes.
I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed: "Lord, you are the great and awesome God. You keep your covenant of faithful love with those who love you and obey your commands.
We have sinned and done wrong. We have been wicked and have rebelled. We have turned away from your commands and your laws.
We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

"Lord, you are always right, but we are covered with shame today. This is true of the people of Judah, those who live in Jerusalem, and all Israel, both near and far, in all the countries where you scattered them because they were unfaithful to you.
LORD, we and our kings, our leaders, and our ancestors are covered with shame, because we have sinned against you.
The Lord our God is merciful and forgiving, even though we have rebelled against him.
We have not obeyed the LORD our God or lived by the laws he gave us through his servants the prophets.

All Israel has broken your law and turned away, refusing to obey you. "So the curses and the oath written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against God.
He has done what he said he would do against us and against our rulers. He has brought great disaster on us. Nothing under the whole heaven has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this disaster has come on us. Yet we have not asked the LORD our God for his favor by turning from our sins and paying attention to your truth.
So the LORD did not hesitate to bring the disaster on us. The LORD our God is right in everything he does, yet we have not obeyed him.
"Now, Lord our God, you brought your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself that lasts to this day. We have sinned. We have done wrong.

Lord, because you always do what is right, please turn your anger and fury away from Jerusalem, your city, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and the sins of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a joke to everyone around us.
"Now, our God, hear the prayers and requests of your servant. For your own sake, Lord, look with favor on your sanctuary that lies in ruins.
My God, turn your ear and listen. Open your eyes and see the ruins of the city that bears your name. We are not asking you because we are good, but because of your great mercy.
Lord, listen! Lord, forgive! Lord, hear and act! For your own sake, my God, do not wait, because your city and your people bear your name."
I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and bringing my request to the LORD my God for his holy mountain.
While I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
He explained things to me and said, "Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.
As soon as you began to pray, an answer was given, and I have come to tell you, because you are greatly loved. So think about the message and understand the vision.

"Seventy weeks have been decreed for your people and your holy city to put an end to rebellion, to finish with sin, to pay for wrongdoing, to bring in a goodness that lasts forever, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most holy place.

"Know and understand this: From the time the command goes out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, comes, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a moat, but in times of trouble.

After the sixty-two weeks, the Anointed One will be cut off and will have nothing. The people of the ruler who will come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood. War will continue until the end, and ruin has been decreed.

He will make a firm agreement with many people for one week. In the middle of that week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of the temple he will set up a disgusting thing that causes ruin, until the end that has been decreed is poured out on the one who causes the ruin."
